question.text: A broker must provide electronic contract notes to clients:

answer.text: As per SEBI guidelines, through email or other electronic means, within the prescribed time with valid digital signature
Only if the client has a demat account
Only in physical format, not electronically

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's electronic contract note framework, brokers are required to issue contract notes to clients within the prescribed time and may do so electronically — typically by email or other secure electronic means — provided the electronic contract notes are authenticated with a valid digital signature and the client has agreed to electronic delivery. The electronic format is treated as equivalent to a physical contract note when these conditions are met. The Trap: Issuance is not contingent on the client having a demat account, is not limited to trades above a monetary threshold like Rs. 50,000, and is certainly not restricted to physical format only. Electronic issuance with digital signature is widely permitted. Note: The specific electronic-contract-note conditions (email/electronic delivery with valid digital signature) are not described in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages discuss timely issuance of contract notes only in general terms. The framing above reflects general SEBI broker-client documentation knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
